types.name: Reciprocal trigonometric ratios and their identities

unknowns.asked: the exact value of sec, cosec or cot at a standard angle
two other ratios, from one of sec, cosec and cot and the quadrant
the solutions of a quadratic in sec or cosec written with tan squared or cot squared
the solutions of an equation in sec squared and tan, to three significant figures

constraints: angles are multiples of 30 or 45 degrees that are not on an axis
a root with |sec x| < 1 or |cosec x| < 1 gives no solution

misconceptions.text: Giving the ratio itself instead of its reciprocal
Replacing tan squared by sec squared and losing the 1
Taking the positive root without looking at the quadrant

unknowns.asked: the exact value of arcsin, arccos or arctan
the exact value of a trigonometric function of an inverse function, and of an inverse function of a trigonometric function
the largest domain and the greatest value of a function built from arcsin or arccos

misconceptions.text: Giving an angle with the right ratio that is outside the principal range

unknowns.asked: the single ratio equal to an expanded compound angle expression
sin(A + B) and cos(A - B) from given ratios of A and B
the exact value of a ratio of 15, 75, 105 or 165 degrees
tan of the double angle and of the angle plus a quarter of pi
tan(A + B), the exact angle A + B and tan 2A
tan x and the solutions of an equation with a compound angle

misconceptions.text: Using the same sign in the expansion of cos(A + B) as in the angle
Writing sin(A + B) as sin A + sin B

types.name: Symmetry relations of the trigonometric functions

unknowns.asked: the ratio of theta equal to a ratio of pi - theta, pi + theta, -theta, pi/2 - theta, pi/2 + theta or 2 pi - theta
four related values from the sine and cosine of an angle
the simplified form of a sum of two related ratios and its exact value

misconceptions.text: Changing the function when the relation keeps it, or keeping it when the relation changes it
